56:1: God Almighty means by His saying, When the Event occurs, that is, when the shout of the Resurrection descends, which is when the Trumpet is blown for the establishment of the Hour. It was also narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, When the Event occurs, meaning: the shout. Ali told us: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, When the Event occurs, the Event, the Calamity, the Deafening Scream, and similar names of the Resurrection. God has made it great and warned His servants about it.
56:2: And His saying, Its occurrence is not false, God Almighty says: The occurrence of the event is not false, nor can it be rejected, nor can it be dual. And false in this context is a source like consequence and well-being. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Its occurrence is not false: meaning it has no duality, no return, and no reversal. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Its occurrence is not false, he said: It is dual.
56:3: And His saying, lowering and raising, God Almighty says: The event will then lower people who were dear to God’s fire in this world. His saying, lowering and raising, means: It raised people who were lowly in this world to the mercy of God and His Paradise. It was also said: It lowered, so that the nearest could hear, and it raised, so that the farthest could hear. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaidullah, meaning Al-Ataki, told us on the authority of Uthman bin Abdullah bin Saraqa: A lowering and raising one: He said: The Hour will lower the enemies of God to Hell and raise the friends of God to Paradise. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, lowering and raising, meaning: It penetrated every plain and mountain until it made everyone, near and far, hear. Then it raised some people to the honor of God and lowered some people to the punishment of God. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, lowering and raising. He said: I made the near and the far hear, lowering some people to the punishment of God and raising some people to the honor of God. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hasan told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, lowering and raising, he said: It lowered and made the nearest hear, and it raised and made the farthest hear. He said: So the near and the far from God were equal. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Lowering and Raising. He said: I heard it from near and far. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh saying: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, lowering and raising, that it lowered so that the nearest could be heard, and it raised so that the farthest could be heard, so the near and the far were equal in it.
56:4: And His statement, When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking, God Almighty says: When the earth is shaken and moved with a movement, from their saying, The arrow shakes in the target, meaning: it shakes and trembles. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Asim told us: Isa told us. Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking, he said: It is shaken. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, When the earth is shaken with a mighty shaking, meaning: shaken with a severe earthquake. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking, meaning: It is shaken with an earthquake.
56:5: And His statement, And the mountains will be crushed to dust, God Almighty says: The mountains will be crushed to dust and will become like powdered flour, which is wet, as God Almighty said: And the mountains will become a heap of sand. Al-Muzzammil 14. Basisa, among the Arabs, means flour and gruel that has been crushed and made into provisions. It was mentioned about a thief from Ghatafan that he wanted to bake bread, but he was afraid that he would hurry up and eat the bread before the flour was ready, and he said, Do not bake bread and bake it in batches. Smooth with the smoothness of the Al-Halsi sheep And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And the mountains will be crushed to dust, meaning: they will be shattered to dust. Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And the mountains will be crushed to dust, he said: They will be shattered. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And the mountains will be dried up completely, he said: Just as gruel dries up. Ahmad bin Amr Al-Basri told me: Hafs bin Omar Al-Adani told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Aban, on the authority of Ikrimah: And the mountains were crushed to dust. He said: They were shattered to dust. Ismail bin Musa bin Bint Al-Suddi told me: Bishr bin Al-Hakam Al-Ahmasi told us on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Salt on the authority of Ismail Al-Suddi and Abu Saleh: And the mountains were crushed. They said: They were shattered. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And the mountains will be dried up. He said: Just as gruel dries up. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about the statement of God, And the mountains will be leveled with a complete leveling, that they will become a heap of sand, as God said. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And the mountains will be crushed, he said: They will be shattered.
56:6: And His saying, And it was scattered dust. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of dust. Some of them said: It is the sun’s rays that enter through the window like dust. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Then it became scattered dust, he said: the rays of the sun. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam bin Amr told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed, scattered dust: He said: The sun’s rays when they enter through the window. He said: Jarir narrated to us on the authority of Mansour on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, Then it was scattered dust, he said: The sun’s rays enter through the window, but it is nothing. Others said: It is the noise of animals. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The blaze of beasts. Others said: It is the sparks of fire that fly away without an eye. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Then it became scattered dust. He said: Dust is what flies from the fire when it is blazing, sparks fly from it, but when it falls, it is nothing. Others said: It is the dry tree that is scattered by the wind. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Then it became scattered dust, meaning the dust of the trees, blown away by the winds to the right and to the left. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, scattered dust, he said: Dust is what the wind scatters of tree debris. We have explained the meaning of haba in other places with evidence, so there is no need to repeat it here. As for his saying scattered, it means scattered.
56:7: God Almighty says: You, O people, are of three types and kinds. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: And you were three groups. He said: The status of people on the Day of Resurrection.
56:8: And His saying, Then the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right? This is a statement from God about the three pairs. He, the Most High, says: And you were three pairs: the companions of the right, the companions of the left, and the foremost. So He made the report about them sufficient to explain them in the way we mentioned, because the words indicate its meaning. So He said, Then the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right? His Prophet Muhammad is amazed by them and said, What are the companions of the right? Al-Waqi’ah 27 Those who will be taken to Paradise by the right, meaning what are the companions of the right?
56:9: And the companions of the left, who are the companions of the left? God Almighty says: And the companions of the left are those who will be taken to the left to the Fire. The Arabs call the left hand: the unlucky, and from this is the saying of A'sha of Banu Tha'labah: Then he lowered his evil hands and quenched them with a black branch, thirstier than the branch of the forelock.
56:10: And His saying, And the foremost, the foremost, they are the third pair, and they are those who were the first to believe in God and His Messenger, and they are the first emigrants. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaid God, meaning Al-Ataki, told us on the authority of Uthman bin Abdullah bin Saraqa, regarding his statement, And you were three groups. He said: Two are in Paradise and one is in Hell. He said: The houris are for the forerunners and the Arabs of their age are for the people of Yemen. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: And you were three groups. He said: People will remain on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Bashar told us: Hudha told us: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, “And you were three groups. The companions of the right - who are the companions of the right? And the companions of the left - who are the companions of the left? And the foremost - the foremost - those are the nearest ones”... to a group of the former peoples * and a few of the latter ones. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “He made the companions of the right hand of the previous nations equal to the companions of the right hand of this nation. And the foremost among the nations were more than the foremost among this nation.” Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Then the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right?: meaning, what are they for, and what has been prepared for them? And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left?: meaning, what are they for, and what has been prepared for them? And the foremost - the foremost?: meaning, from every nation. Yunus told us: Ibn Wahb told us: I heard Ibn Zayd say: I found desire to be of three types. A person makes his desire his knowledge, so his desire prevails over his knowledge, and his desire subdues his knowledge until knowledge with desire is ugly and humiliating, and knowledge is humiliating to desire, and is overwhelming and subduing. So the one who has placed desire and knowledge in his heart, this is one of the people of Hellfire. And if he is one for whom God wants good, he will awaken and become aware, and he will be a helper to knowledge over desire until God makes knowledge prevail over desire. So if the state of the believer improves and his path is straight, then desire will be humiliating and knowledge will be overwhelming and subduing. And if he is one for whom God wants good, he ends his work by making knowledge prevail, so he takes his life, and his knowledge is the dominant one and he is the one who acts upon it, and his desire is humiliating and ugly, and he has no share or action in that. The third: the one whose desire God has made ugly with his knowledge, so his desire does not hope to overcome knowledge or to have half or a share with it. This is the third, and he is the best of you all, and he is the one about whom God, the Exalted, said in Surat al-Waqi’ah 56:And you were three pairs. He said: So two pairs will be in Paradise and one pair will be in Hellfire. He said: The one who is foremost is the one who is… Knowledge is often for desire, and the other: the one whom God has sealed with knowledge prevailing over desire, these two are a pair in Paradise, and the other: his desire is overpowering his knowledge, so this is the pair in Hell. The Arab scholars differed about the subject of the verb the companions of the right and the companions of the left. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The predicate of his statement, So the companions of the right is What are the companions of the right? and the companions of the left is What are the companions of the left? He said: And Zaid says: How strong Zaid is.” Another said: His statement, What are the companions of the right? The sentence is not its predicate, but the second refers back to the first and is an expression of astonishment. So it is as if he said: Who are the companions of the right? What is the calamity? What is the inevitable? So the dual refers back to the first and is an expression of astonishment. Astonishment has the meaning of predicate. If it were an interrogative, it would not be permissible for it to be predicate of the subject because an interrogative cannot be a predicate and a predicate cannot be an interrogative, and astonishment can be a predicate, so it was predicate of the subject. His statement, Zaid and what Zaid can only be from two statements because the letter and does not enter into the predicate of the subject, as if he said: This is Zaid and what is he? Meaning: How strong he is and how knowledgeable he is. The people of interpretation differed regarding the two meanings of his statement, and the foremost, the foremost. Some of them said: They are those who prayed towards the two qiblas. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Kharijah, on the authority of Qurrah, on the authority of Ibn Sirin: And the foremost are the foremost are those who prayed towards the two Qiblahs. Others said about this: Abdul Karim bin Abi Umair told me: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us: Abu Amr told us: Uthman bin Abi Sawda told us: And the foremost ones are the foremost ones are the first of them to go to the mosques and the quickest of them to go out in the way of God. The nominative case in the two previous ones is from two aspects: One of them is that the first is nominative with the second, and the meaning of the speech then is: And the first to precede, just as it is said: The first to precede, and the second is that it is nominative with those who are brought near, the Most High says: Those are the ones whom God will bring near to Him on the Day of Resurrection when He admits them into Paradise.
56:12: And his saying, In the gardens of bliss, means: In the orchards of eternal bliss.
56:13: God Almighty says: A group of past nations and a few from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they are the last. They were called the last because they are the last of the nations.
56:15: On woven couches He says: On woven couches, some of which have been inserted into others, just as the rings of a shield are woven doubled over each other. From this comes the saying of Al-A'sha: And the fabric of David's loom is woven, and it is driven with the tribe, one by one. And from it is the lining of the camel, which is the lining of the belts if some of it is woven on top of the other in doubled order like the rings of the armor. It was said: Wadhin, but it is Mawdoon, inflected from Mafool to Fa’il, just as it was said: Qatil for Maqtool. It was reported that some Arabs heard the bricks placed one on top of the other, meaning a weak mashraj. It was said that it has decorated beds because it is woven with gold and jewels. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Mu’ail told us: Sufyan told us: Hisin told us on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas: On adorned couches. He said: Decorated with gold. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Hussain, on the authority of Mujahid: On adorned couches. He said: adorned with gold. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, On lined couches, he said: He means the lined couches. Hanad told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Al-Mawduna is the one covered with gold. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, On adorned couches, he said: adorned with pearls and rubies. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, adorned, he said: adorned with gold. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, On lined couches. The lined one is the one that is lined, and it is the softest of couches. Ibn Bashar told us: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, On lined couches, he said: A woven sand couch. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, On woven couches, “Waddin” means interlacing and weaving. He said: Its middle is a woven mesh. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, On couches lined up, “lined up” means the one woven with leather. That is, the woven. Others said: Rather, it means that it is arranged. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, on lined couches, meaning: arranged in rows.
56:16: And His statement, Reclining on them, facing each other, God Almighty says: Reclining on lined couches, facing each other, not looking at the backs of one another. Ibn Hamid also told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, On thrones facing each other, he said: One of them should not look at the back of his companion. He mentioned that in Abdullah’s reading it is, Reclining on them facing each other. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq: In the recitation of Abdullah, meaning Ibn Mas`ud, it is: reclining on them, facing each other. We have explained this in other places and mentioned what is in it of the narration.
56:17: And His statement, There will circulate among them immortal youths, God Almighty says: There will circulate among these forerunners whom God has brought near in the Gardens of Bliss, youths of the same age who do not change and do not die. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Immortal means they will not die. Others said: He meant that they were covered with earrings and bracelets. What is more correct in this regard is the statement of those who said that its meaning is: that they do not change and do not die, because that is the most obvious of its two meanings. The Arabs say about a man who has grown old and has not combed his hair: he is immortal, but it is a verbal noun from immortality.
56:18: And his saying, with cups and pitchers. Cups is the plural of cup, which is a pitcher that has a wide head and does not have a trunk. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told us: My uncle told us: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, with cups, he said: The cups are the silver jugs. Ibn Bashar told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: With cups and pitchers. He said: A pitcher is something that has spouts, and cups have spouts. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Cups do not have ears. Yaqub told us: Ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of Abu Raja’ who said: Al-Hasan was asked about cups. He said: They are the pitchers from which water is poured for them. Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa’ib told us: Ibn Idris told us: I heard my father say: Abu Salih, the companion of al-Kalbi, passed by. My father said: Al-Hasan said to me while I was sitting, Ask him. I said: What are cups? He said: Silver jugs with round mouths and pitchers with spouts. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: With cups. He said: It has no handles or ears. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, with cups and pitchers. The cups from which water is scooped do not have spouts and are smaller than pitchers. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, with cups and pitchers, he said: The cups that are smaller than pitchers do not have handles. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: The cups are jars that do not have handles, and in Nabataean they are kubah, and it was narrated to me by Al-A’sha, who said: A delicious, creamy dish with a hint of butter between its cup and ear As for the jugs: they are the ones that have handles. His saying, And a cup of flowing water, and a cup of wine from a flowing drink that is apparent to the eyes. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And a cup of pure wine, he said: Wine. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And a cup of flowing wine, meaning of running wine. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And a cup from a flowing spring, the cup means wine. Abu Sinan told us: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And a cup of flowing wine, he said: Running wine.
56:19: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salamah ibn Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, similarly. His saying, They will not get a headache from it, means: Their heads will not get a headache from drinking it and thus become intoxicated. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ismail bin Musa Al-Suddi told me: Sharik told us on the authority of Salim on the authority of Saeed, regarding his statement, They will not have a headache from it, he said: Their heads will not be headaches. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: They do not suffer a headache from it means it does not cause a headache. Ibn Bashar told us: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us on the authority of Qatada: They will not have a headache from it. He said: Their heads will not be broken. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid: They will not have a headache from it. He said: Their heads will not be broken. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, They will not suffer a headache from it, meaning: a headache. And his saying, nor do they bleed. The reciters differed in its reading. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it nor do they bleed with a fat-ha on the zay, and they explained that by saying that their minds will not bleed. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it nor do they bleed with a kasra on the zay, meaning: nor will their drink run out. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of this in the same way that the reciters differed in it. We mentioned the difference in their statements in this and explained the correct statement in Surat as-Saffat, so that made it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. However, I will remember the statement of some of them in this place so that no one will think that its meaning in this place is different from its meaning there. Some of them said: It means do not let their minds bleed. Ismail bin Musa told us: Sharik told us on the authority of Salim on the authority of Sa’id: And they do not lose their minds. He said: Their minds do not lose their minds. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid: And they do not lose their minds. He said: Their minds do not lose their minds. Ibn Hamid told us again and said: Their minds will not go away. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, nor will they be exhausted, that their minds will not be exhausted. Bishr told us: Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, nor shall they be overcome by insanity, he said: No one shall be overcome by his mind. Ibn Bashar told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us regarding his statement, nor shall they be overcome by blood, they said: No one shall lose his mind. Ibn Bashar told us: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us on the authority of Qatada regarding the statement of God, nor shall they be overcome by blood, he said: Their minds shall not be overcome.
56:20: And His statement: And fruit of whatever they choose, God Almighty says: And these immortal youths will circulate among these forerunners with fruit from the fruits that they choose for themselves from Paradise and that their souls desire.
56:21: And the meat of birds of whatever they desire. He says: And they will also be given to them the meat of birds of whatever they desire, from the birds that their souls desire.
56:22: The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, And houris of wide-eyed beauty. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the Medinans recited it as and houris of wide-eyed beauty in the accusative case, following its parsing like the parsing of what preceded it of fruit and meat, even though that is not something that is circumambulated. But since its intended meaning was known, the latter followed the former in parsing, as some poets said: If the prostitutes appear one day and raise their eyebrows and eyes The eyes are lined with kohl, but only the eyebrows are lined. So, in parsing, it is returned to the eyebrows so that the listener will understand the meaning of that, as the other said: You hear a rumbling sound from his entrails, and a grinding sound from his hands. Al-Jasah: roughness in the hand that does not hear. Some of the readers of Medina and Mecca and some of the people of Basra read it in the nominative case, and houris of wide-eyed women, as a subject, and they said: The houris of wide-eyed women are not to be walked around with, so it is permissible to connect them in the syntactic sense to fruit and meat, but it is in the nominative case, meaning: and with them are houris of wide-eyed women, or they have houris of wide-eyed women. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is: They are two well-known readings, each of which has been read by a group of readers, despite their meanings being close. So whichever of the two readings the reader reads, he is correct. Al-Hoor is a group of Hawra’, which is the pure whiteness of the eye and its intense blackness. Al-Ayn is the plural of ‘Ayna’, which is the clear, beautiful eye.
56:23: And his saying, Like hidden pearls, means: They are, in the purity of their whiteness and beauty, like hidden pearls that have been preserved in a treasure chest.
56:24: And His statement, A reward for what they used to do, God Almighty says: A reward for them from God for the deeds they used to do in this world and in exchange for their obedience to Him. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said? Who said that? Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And houris with wide, beautiful eyes. He said: “Intensely black: the blackness of the eyes. Intensely white: the whiteness of the eyes.” He said: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: And houris with large, beautiful eyes. He said: White eyes. He said: Big eyes. Ibn Abbas Al-Duri told us: Hajjaj told us: Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ata Al-Khurasani on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Houri is the one with black eyes. Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Ibrahim bin Muhammad Al-Aslami told us, on the authority of Ibad bin Mansour Al-Baji, that he heard Al-Hasan Al-Basri say: The houris are the righteous women of the children of Adam. He said: Ibrahim bin Muhammad told us on the authority of Laith bin Abi Salim, who said: I was informed that the houris were created from saffron. Al-Hasan bin Yazid Al-Tahhan told us: Aisha, the wife of Laith, told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The houris were created from saffron. Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me: Amr bin Saad told us: I heard Laith tell me on the authority of Mujahid who said: The houris were created from saffron. Others said: Rather, the meaning of his saying Houri is that the eye is perplexed by them. Who said that? Abu Hisham told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid: And beautiful women with wide, beautiful eyes. He said: The eye is dazzled by them. And in a similar manner to what we said in the interpretation of his saying, like pearls, the people of interpretation said, and the trace came from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman told us: Ahmad bin Al-Faraj Al-Sadfi Al-Dimyati told us, on the authority of Amr bin Hashim, on the authority of Ibn Abi Karima, on the authority of Hisham bin Hassan, on the authority of his mother, on the authority of Umm Salama, who said: I said, O Messenger of God, tell me about the statement of God, Like hidden pearls. He said: Their purity is like the purity of pearls in shells that are not touched by hands.
56:25: And His statement, They will hear therein no idle talk or sinful talk, means: They will hear therein no false speech or sinful talk. He says: There is nothing in it that will make them sinful. Some of the people of Basra who were knowledgeable about the generosity of the Arabs used to say, They do not hear any idle talk or sinful talk there. Sinful talk is not heard, but rather idle talk is heard, as it was said: I ate bread and milk, and milk is not eaten, so it was permissible because there was something with it that could be eaten.
56:26: And his saying, "Except for the saying, 'Peace, peace,'" means: They will not hear therein any speech except for the saying of 'Peace, peace,' meaning safer than what you dislike. There are two views on the accusative of his saying, "Peace, peace," if you wish, you can make it dependent on the saying, and then peace would be the saying, so it is as if it was said: They will not hear therein any idle talk or sinful talk except 'Peace, peace,' but they hear 'Peace, peace.' The second view is that it is accusative because of the saying occurring upon it, so its meaning then is: Except for the saying of 'Peace, peace,' so the 'nun' is the accusative of his saying, "Peace, peace," because it was said upon it.
56:27: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, And the companions of the right hand, and they are the ones who will be taken on the Day of Resurrection to the right hand, who were given their books in their right hands, O Muhammad. What are the companions of the right hand? What is it, what do they have, and what good has been prepared for them? It has been said that they are the children of the believers. Who said that? Muhammad bin Muammar told us: Abu Hisham Al-Makhzumi told us: Abdul Wahid told us: Al-A’mash told us: Uthman bin Qais told us that he heard Zadan Abu Amr say: I heard Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, say: And the companions of the right hand - who are the companions of the right hand? He said: The companions of the right hand are the children of the believers. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right? meaning, what will they have and what has been prepared for them? Then he began the story about what will be prepared for them in Paradise and what will be their state when they enter it.
56:28: He said: They are among thornless lote trees, meaning: among the fruit of a thorny lote tree, bearing a burden whose share has been lost. The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of it. Some of them said: By al-makhdud he means: that which is cut by thorns, so there are no thorns in it. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Thornless lote trees, he said: Its thorns are its burden from the load. It is also said: It is thorned until its thorns are gone, so there are no thorns in it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us on the authority of his father: In a lote tree with no thorns. He said: Muhammad ibn Ikrimah claimed that he said: It has no thorns. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, In thornless lote trees, he said, It has no thorns. Ibn Bashar told us: Hudhah bin Khalifa told us: Aouf told us on the authority of Qasama bin Zuhair regarding his statement, In thornless lote trees, he said: It is thornless, so there are no thorns in it. Abu Hamid Al-Himsi Ahmad bin Al-Mughira told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us: Amr bin Abdullah Al-Ahmosi told us on the authority of Al-Safar bin Naseer regarding the statement of God Almighty, In thornless lote trees, he said: It has no thorns, so there are no thorns in it. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, In thornless lote trees, he said: We used to say that it means the one with no thorns. Ibn Bashar told us: Sulayman told us: Qatada told us regarding His statement, In thornless lote trees, he said: It has no thorns. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Ikrimah: In a lote tree with no thorns. He said: It has no thorns. Ibn Hamid told me about it again on the authority of Marhan with this chain of transmission on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: It has no thorns, it is the honored one. Others said: Rather, he meant that he was the one who was honored and carried. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Makhdud said: They say this is a burden. Muhammad bin Sinan Al-Qazzaz told me: Abu Hudhayfah told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: In thornless lote trees. He said: The venerated ones. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: In a lote tree with thorns. He said: The venerated one. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, In thornless lote trees, meaning: venerated. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, In a lote tree with thorns, he said: Its fruit is larger than a jug.
56:29: And his saying, And Talh Mandhud, as for the reciters, they read that with a ha', And Talh Mandhud, and this is how it is in the copies of the Qur’ans of the people of the regions. It was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he used to read And Talh Mandhud with an ayn. Abdullah bin Muhammad Al-Zuhri told us: Sufyan told us: Zakariya told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Saad, on the authority of his father, may God be pleased with him, who read it It came out arranged. Saeed bin Yahya Al-Amawi told us: My father told me: Mujahid told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Saad, on the authority of Qais bin Saad, who said: A man read in the presence of Ali, And Talh trees in layers. Ali said: What is the matter with Talh? It is only And Talh trees in layers. Then he read, Its fruits are tender Ash-Shu’ara’ 148. We said: Should we not change it? He said: The Qur’an is neither contradicted nor changed today. As for Talh, Al-Mu’ammar bin Al-Muthanna used to say: Among the Arabs, it is a large tree with many thorns. And he recited to one of the hadith scholars: Her guide gave her good report and said, Tomorrow is the date palm and the habala. As for the people of interpretation from the Companions and the Followers, they say: It is the banana. Humaid bin Masada told us: Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us: Sulayman al-Tamimi told us on the authority of Abu Saeed, a client of the Banu Ruqash, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the talh tree, and he said: It is the banana. Yaqub told me: Hisham told us: Sulayman al-Tamimi told us: Abu Saeed al-Raqashi told us: I said to Ibn Abbas: What is the arranged talh? He said: It is the... Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us on the authority of his father: Abu Sa’id al-Raqashi told us: Ibn Abbas said: And bananas in layers. He said: Bananas. He said: Mahrān narrated to us on the authority of Sufyān on the authority of al-Kalbi on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Sa`īd on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: And Talh trees in layers. He said: The Moor. Yaqoub told me: Hisham told us: Abu Bishr told us on the authority of a man from Basra that he heard Ibn Abbas say about the arranged talh, it is the banana. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And bananas in layers, he said: Your bananas, because they were amazed by the shade and shade of its bananas and lote trees. Muhammad bin Sinan told us: Abu Hudhayfah told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement, And bananas in layers, he said: Bananas. Ibn Bashar told us: Hawdhah bin Khalifa told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Qasama, who said: The arranged talh is the banana. He said: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us on the authority of Qatada regarding the statement of God, And bananas in layers, he said: Bananas. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: And bananas in layers. He said: Bananas. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And bananas in layers. We used to say that it meant bananas. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And bananas in layers, that God knows best, except that the people of Yemen call bananas talh. His saying arranged means that some of it was arranged on top of some and some of it was gathered together. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And bananas in layers, he said: Some of them on top of each other. Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And banana trees in layers, is piled up because they are amazed by the appearance and shade of its banana and lote trees.
56:30: And his saying, and an extended shade, means: They are in a permanent shade that the sun does not remove or erase, and everything that has no end is extended, as Labid said: Survival prevailed, and I was not defeated, a long, everlasting, extended age The hadiths came in a similar manner to what we said about that, and the people of knowledge said it. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun: And an extended shadow. He said: Five hundred thousand years. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us: Ismail told us, on the authority of Abu Khalid, on the authority of Ziyad, the client of Banu Makhzum, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree under whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years. Read, if you wish, ‘and an extended shade.’” That reached Ka’b, so he said: He has spoken the truth, and by Him who sent down the Torah on the tongue of Moses and the Criterion on the tongue of Muhammad, if a man were to ride his right hand or its trunk and then circle around the base of that tree, he would not reach it until he fell down in old age. Indeed, God planted it with His hand and breathed into it of His spirit. Its branches are beyond the Surah of Paradise. There is no river in Paradise except that it flows from the base of that tree.” Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid on the authority of Ziyad, a client of Banu Makhzum, that he heard Abu Hurairah say, then he mentioned something similar except that he said: And there is no river in Paradise. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun: And an extended shadow. He said: A journey of seventy thousand years. Yunus told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Abu Yahya bin Sulayman told me, on the authority of Hilal bin Ali, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years. Read, if you wish, ‘and an extended shade.’” Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein bin Muhammad told us on the authority of Ziyad, who said: I heard Abu Hurairah say: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. And if you wish, recite: ‘And an extended shade.’” Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Shu`bah told us on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider can travel for seventy or one hundred years. It is the tree of immortality.” Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Dawud told us: Imran told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. He said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Waki` narrated to us on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly. Abu Kurayb told us: Abda and Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. And read, if you wish, His statement: ‘and an extended shade.’” Abu Kuraib told us: Firdaws told us: Laith told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Saeed, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years. Abu Kuraib told us: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the same. Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us: Khalid bin Al-Harith told us: Aouf told us on the authority of Al-Hasan: It has reached me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Khalid told us: Aouf told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and similarly on the authority of Khalas. Abu Kuraib told us: Abu Bakr told us: Abu Hasin told us: We were at a door in a place whose meaning was Abu Salih and Shuqaiq, meaning Ad-Dhabi. Abu Salih spoke and said: Abu Hurairah told me: There is a tree in Paradise, in the shade of which a rider can travel for seventy years. Abu Salih said: Do you lie about Abu Hurairah? He said: I do not lie about Abu Hurairah, but I lie about you. He said: There will be corruption on the reciters that day. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us on the authority of Qatada: And an extended shade. He said: Anas bin Malik told us: There is a tree in Paradise in whose shade a rider would be pleased for a hundred years without crossing it. He said: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And an extended shade. Qatada said, Anas bin Malik told us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, something similar.
56:31: And His saying, and poured water, God Almighty says: And in it also poured water, meaning poured and flowing in a way other than a groove. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan: And poured water. He said: It flows in a groove other than a trench.
56:32: He says, And abundant fruit, neither forbidden nor prohibited. God Almighty says: In it are abundant fruits, and none of them that they desire at any given time will be cut off from them, just as the fruits of summer are cut off in winter in this world. And they will not be prevented from it or come between them and it by the thorns of its trees or its distance from them, just as the fruits of this world are prevented from many of those who desire them by their distance from the tree or by the thorns on its trees. But if one of them desires them, they will fall into his mouth or come close to him so that he can take them with his hand. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: We mentioned the story before and we will mention some of it: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us: Qatada told us regarding his statement, Neither cut off nor forbidden, he said: Neither thorns nor distance prevent it.
56:34: And His saying, And raised couches, God Almighty says: And they will have therein raised, long couches, one above the other, as one would say: a raised building. And as Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Rashdin bin Saad told us, on the authority of Amr bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Daraj Abi Al-Samh, on the authority of Abi Al-Haitham, on the authority of Abi Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement, And raised couches, he said: Their height is like that between the sky and the earth, and the distance between the sky and the earth is a journey of five hundred years. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Amr told us, on the authority of Darraj, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: And raised mattresses. By the One in Whose hand is my soul, its being raised… then he mentioned something similar.
56:35: And His statement, Indeed, We created them a special creation * And made them virgins * Lovely. God Almighty says: Indeed, We created them a special creation, then We brought them into existence. Abu Ubaidah said: He means by that: the houris mentioned before, so he said, And houris with large, beautiful eyes * Like hidden pearls.... Indeed, We created them a special creation. Al-Akhfash said: He implied them and did not mention them before that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, We created them a new creation. He said: We created them a creation. Abu Kurayb told us: Muawiyah bin Hisham told us, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Jabir al-Ja’fi, on the authority of Yazid bin Murrah, on the authority of Salamah bin Yazid, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding this verse: Indeed, We created them a special creation. He said: From the previously married and the virgins. And His saying, So We made them virgins, means: So We made them virgins after they had been. Hamid narrated to us, on the authority of Mihran, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Yazid bin Aban al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We created them a special creation. He said: Old women who were blind and lame in this world. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Yazid bin Abaan al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘We created them as a creation.’ He said: We created old women who were blind and lame in this world.” Omar bin Ismail bin Mujallid told us: Muhammad bin Rabi’ah Al-Kalabi told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah Al-Rabdhi, on the authority of Yazid Al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding His statement, ‘Indeed, We created them a special creation,’ he said: Among them are the old women who were blind and lame in this world.” Suwar bin Abdullah bin Dawud told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah al-Rabdhi, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement, Indeed, We created them a special creation, he said: They are those who were old, blind, and without vision in this world. Hadith Ibn Bashar said: Amr bin Asim told us: Al-Mu'tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Safwan bin Mahraz, regarding His statement, Indeed, We created them a special creation * And made them virgins, he said: So they are the weak, bleary-eyed ones. Ibn Bashar told us: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us: Qatada told us regarding His statement, Indeed, We created them a special creation * And made them virgins, he said: Among them are the weak and weak-willed ones whom God created in this creation. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, We created them a special creation. Qatada said: Safwan bin Majraz used to say: Among them are the weak and the weak. God made them as you hear. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: His statement, virgins, means: virgins. Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Sadfi al-Dimyati narrated to us, on the authority of Amr ibn Hashim, on the authority of Ibn Abi Karima, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Hassan, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that she said: I said, O Messenger of God, tell me about the statement of God, “Indeed, We created them a special creation. And made them virgins, * Loving of equal age * For the companions of the right hand.” He said: They are those who were taken in this world as old women, with blemishes and black hair. God created them after they had grown old and made them virgins. Abu Ubaid Al-Wasabi told us: Muhammad bin Hamir told us: Thabit bin Ajlan told us: I heard Saeed bin Jubair narrating on the authority of Ibn Abbas in: Indeed, We created them a special creation, and made them virgins, loving and equal in age. He said: They are from the children of Adam, your women in this world. God creates them as virgins, loving and equal in age. And His saying, Arabs, God Almighty says: So We made them virgins, coquettish, beloved to their husbands, who treat them well. It is the plural of arub, the singular of which is arub, just as the singular of rasul is rasool, and the singular of qatf is qatuf. From this is the saying of Labid: In the borders, there is a beautiful, not obscene, Arab woman with beautiful rumps that blinds the eyes. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Ismail bin Aban and Ismail bin Subaih told us on the authority of Abu Idris on the authority of Thawr bin Zaid on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Arabs of equal age he said: the one who is in a good mood. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Arabs, meaning: lovers. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Arabs, he said: Arab women who are affectionate and affectionate towards their husbands. Sulayman bin Abdullah al-Ghailani told me, he said: Thana’ Ayoub told us, he said: Qura told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said: Arabs: the lover. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of `Ikrimah, that he said about this verse, Arabs. He said: He said: The coquettish Arabs. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Samak bin Ikrimah, who said: It is the coquettish one. Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Amara bin Abi Hafsa told us on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement, Arabs, he said: Arab women. Ali bin Al-Hassan Al-Azdi told me: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Taimi, on the authority of Salih bin Hayyan, on the authority of Abu Buraidah, Arabs, who said: doubt is in one language and coquettishness is in the language of Medina. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us: I heard Ibrahim al-Taimi, meaning Ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of Salih Ibn Hayyan, on the authority of Abu Yazid, in a similar manner. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Uthman ibn Bashar, on the authority of Tamim ibn Hudlam, regarding his statement, Arabs, he said: The woman’s good behavior. Yaqub told me: Hisham told us: Mughira told us on the authority of Uthman bin Bashar on the authority of Tamim bin Hudlam regarding Araba: He said: Araba is the beautiful woman who is a wife. He said: The Arabs used to say about a woman who was beautiful in her husband: She is a beautiful woman. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Usama bin Zabad bin Aslam, on the authority of his father: Arabs means good speech. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Lovers. He said: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid and Ikrimah, the same. He said: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Mujahid, Arabs, he said: The beloved Arabs. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid: Arabs. He said: Arabs are lovers. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salim Al-Futtas, on the authority of Saeed bin Hassan, similarly. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ghalib Abu al-Hudhayl, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr: Arabs means Arab women who desire their husbands. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Al-Mubarak bin Fadala, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: Those who desire their husbands. He said: Ibn Idris told us: Uthman bin Al-Aswad told us on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaid God, who said: The Arab woman is the one who desires her husband. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair, Arabs. He said: The Arab woman is the one who desires her husband. Do you not see that a man says to a female camel: She is Arab? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Arabs means love for their husbands. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Arab women of equal age, meaning: They love their husbands with intense love. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say: The Arabs are the beloved ones. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Arabs of equal age, he said: They are beloved to their husbands. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about his statement, Arabs, that he said: The Arabs are the ones who speak well. Ibn Al-Barqi told us: Amr bin Abi Salamah told us: Al-Awza’i was asked about Arabs. He said: I heard Yahya say: They are the lovers. Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman told us: Muhammad bin Al-Faraj Al-Sadfi Al-Dimyati told us, on the authority of Amr bin Hashim, on the authority of Abu Karima, on the authority of Hisham bin Hassan, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of his mother, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said: I said, O Messenger of God, tell me about His statement, Arabs of equal age. He said: Arabs who are in love and are fond of each other, born together.” Muhammad bin Hafs Abu Ubaid Al-Wasabi told me: Muhammad bin Hamir told us: Thabit bin Ajlan told us: I heard Saeed bin Jubair narrating on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Arabs, and Arab means longing. The reciters differed in reading this. Some of the reciters of Medina and some of the reciters of Kufa read it as Araba with a damma on the ‘ayn and the ra’. Some of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it as Araba with a damma on the ‘ayn and a soft ra’. This is the language of Tamim and Bakr. The damma on the two letters is the more correct of the two readings, because I mentioned that it is the plural of ‘arub, even if it is fa’ul or fa’al or fa’al, if it is pluralized, it is a plural on fa’al with a damma on the fa’ and the ‘ayn, whether masculine or feminine. Softening the ‘ayn is permissible, even though what I mentioned is the most extreme of the two statements in terms of lightening. His saying of the same age means that they are of the same age, and one of them is tarb, just as one says similar and similar. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Al-Harith told me: Muhammad bin Rabia told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Sabur, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Atrab means those of equal status. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, of equal age, he said: similar. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Atraban means: of the same age. Ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, similarly. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, of equal age, that he said: of equal age means those of equal level.
56:38: And His statement, For the companions of the right, God Almighty says: We created these virgins whose characteristics He described for those who will be taken to the right from the place of reckoning to Paradise.
56:39: God Almighty says: Those who have this honor, the description of which is in these verses, are two groups, two nations, and two sects: A group from the first meaning a group from those who passed before the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And a group from the last meaning: And a group from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the people of interpretation said this. He mentioned the story. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan, who said: Al-Hasan said: A group of the first of the nations, and a group of the last: the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated: Saeed narrated: Qatada narrated: Al-Hasan narrated from the hadith of Imran ibn Husayn from Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, who said: “We talked with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) one night until we were bored with talking, then we returned to our families. When morning came, we went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘The prophets were presented to me last night with their followers from their nations. A prophet would come with a group from his nation, a prophet with a group from his nation, a prophet with a man from his nation, and a prophet with no one from his nation with him from his people, until Moses ibn Imran came to me with a large group of the Children of Israel. When I saw them, I was amazed, so I said: ‘O Lord, who are these?’ He said: ‘This is your brother Moses ibn Imran and those with him from the Children of Israel.’ I said: ‘O Lord, where are my nation?’ It was said: ‘Look to your right and there are the gates of Mecca blocked with the faces of men.’ I said: ‘Who are these?’ It was said: ‘These are your nation.’ It was said: ‘Are you satisfied?’ I said: ‘O Lord, I am satisfied.’” O Lord, are you satisfied? It was said: Look to your left and if the horizon is blocked with the faces of men, then I said: O Lord, who are these? It was said: These are your nation. It was said: Are you satisfied? I said: I am satisfied, O Lord, I am satisfied. It was said: With these are seventy thousand from your nation who will enter Paradise without being called to account. He said: Then ‘Ukasha bin Mihsan, a man from Banu Asad bin Khuzaymah, stood up and said: O Prophet of God, call upon your Lord to make me one of them. He said: O God, make him one of them. Then another man stood up and said: O Prophet of God, call upon your Lord to make me one of them. He said: ‘Ukasha has preceded you in that. Then the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, if you are able to be among the seventy, then be. If you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the horizon. If you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the horizon, for I saw then people who were very greedy, or he said, were greedy. He said: Then the believers turned back, or he said, we turned back on these seventy, and it became part of their affair that they said: We see them as people who were born in Islam and they did not stop practicing it until they died upon it. Their talk reached the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: It is not like that, but they are the ones who do not seek ruqyah, nor cauterize, nor take omens, and they put their trust in their Lord. It was mentioned that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on that day: I hope that those of my nation who follow me will be a quarter of the people of Paradise. So we said, Allahu Akbar. Then he said: I hope that you will be half. So we said, Allahu Akbar. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: A group from the first peoples * And a group from the last peoples. Abu Kuraib narrated: Al-Hasan bin Bishr Al-Bajali narrated from Al-Hakam bin Abdul-Malik from Qatada from Al-Hasan from Imran bin Husayn from Abdullah bin Masoud who said: We talked one night in the presence of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until we were bored or more than we were. Then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: The gates of Mecca were blocked with men’s faces. He also said: I saw people in his presence arguing a lot. We said: Who are these seventy thousand? We agreed that they are people who were born in Islam and will die in Islam. We mentioned that to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he said: No, but they are people who do not cauterize. He also said: Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise. His companions said: Allahu Akbar. Then he said: I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise. His companions said: Allahu Akbar. Then he said: I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. Then he recited: A group of the first peoples * And a group of the last peoples. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, who said: All of them are in Paradise. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, that it was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Would you be satisfied to be a quarter of the people of Paradise? They said: Yes. He said: Would you be satisfied to be a third of the people of Paradise? They said: Yes. He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. Then he recited this verse: A group from the first peoples * And a group from the last peoples. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Badil ibn Ka’b that he said: The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, eighty of which are from this nation. There are two aspects to raising the word three: one is the resumption and the other is by saying: For the people of the right are two-thirds, a third from the first. It has been narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a report from a reliable source from him that he said: The two-thirds together are from my nation. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abaan bin Abi Ayyash, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A group from the first and a group from the last. He said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are both from my nation.”
56:41: And His saying, And the companions of the left - who are the companions of the left? God Almighty says, admiring His Prophet Muhammad from the people of Hellfire. And the companions of the left? Who will be taken to the left from the place of reckoning to Hellfire. What are the companions of the left? What will they have and what has been prepared for them. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying, And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left? meaning, what will they have and what has been prepared for them?
56:42: And his saying, in poisonous water and scalding water, means: They are in the poisonous water and scalding water of Hell.
56:43: And His statement, And a shade of black smoke, God Almighty says: And a shade of intense black smoke. The Arabs say for everything that is described as intense black: black and black. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abi Al-Shawarib told me: Abd Al-Wahid Ibn Ziyad told us: Sulayman Al-Shaibani told us: Yazid Ibn Al-Asamm told us: I heard Ibn Abbas say about and the shade of al-Dukhan 44:It is the shade of smoke. Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told us: Qubaysah bin Laith told us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Yazid bin Al-Asamm, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Idris told us: I heard Al-Shaibani on the authority of Yazid bin Al-Asamm on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Shaibani, on the authority of Yazid ibn al-Asamm, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And a shade of black smoke. He said: Smoke. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, and a shade of scalding smoke, meaning: of scalding smoke. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of `Ikrimah, that he said regarding this verse, And a shade of black smoke, he said: Smoke. Abu Kuraib told us: Othman told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Malik, regarding his statement, and a shade of scorching smoke, he said: scalding smoke. Saeed bin Yahya Al-Amawi told us: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Malik, with the same chain of transmission. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid: And a shade of smoke. He said: Smoke. He said: Jarir narrated to us on the authority of Mansour on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, From a scalding smoke, he said: From scalding smoke. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Sulayman al-Shaybani, on the authority of Yazid ibn al-Asamm, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And a shade of black smoke. They said: Smoke. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And a shade of black smoke. He said: Of smoke. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And the shade of a black smoke. We used to say that it was the shade of smoke. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, and a shade of scorching heat, that the shade of smoke is the smoke of Hell. Some scholars have claimed this.
56:44: And His statement, Neither cool nor generous, the Almighty says: That shade is not cool like the coolness of the shades of other things, but it is hot because it is smoke from the blazing fire of Hell, and it is not generous because it is painful for whoever seeks shade under it. The Arabs follow every attribute of praise that is negated from it with the negation of generosity, so they say: This food is neither good nor generous, this meat is neither fat nor generous, and this house is neither clean nor generous. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told me: Al-Nadr told us: Juwaybir told us on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement, Neither cool nor generous, he said: Every drink that is not sweet is not generous. Qatada used to say about this: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Neither cool nor generous. He said: Neither cool of home nor generous of appearance.
56:45: And His statement, Indeed, they were before that in luxury, God Almighty says: Indeed, those whose characteristics He described from the companions of the left were, before the punishment of God that befell them in this world, in luxury, meaning in comfort. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us on the authority of Ali on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They were, before that, in luxury. He said: pampered.
56:46: And His saying, And they persisted in the great sin, God Almighty says: And they persisted in the great sin. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: They persist means they persist. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: They apply anointing or they apply it constantly. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And they persisted, that they did not repent nor seek forgiveness. Persistence in sin among the Arabs means persisting in it and not giving it up. His saying, for the great perjury, means: for the great sin, which is polytheism. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: On the great oath he said: On the sin. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Abu Tamila told us: Ubaid bin Sulayman told us on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement, The great perjury, he said: Polytheism. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, upon great perjury, meaning: polytheism. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: The great perjury means the sin. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said: And they persisted in the great perjury. He said: The great perjury is the great sin. He said: And that great sin is polytheism. They neither repented nor sought forgiveness. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And they persisted in the great oath, which is polytheism. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: On the great oath he said: the great sin.
56:47: God the Almighty says: And they used to say, out of disbelief in the Resurrection and denial that God gives life to His creation after their death, When we are dust in our graves after our death and rotten bones, will we then be resurrected from them [as we were] before death, or our forefathers who were before us? And they are the first. God says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these al-Nas 114:Indeed, the first of your forefathers and the last of you and others besides you will be gathered to an appointed time on a known Day, and that is the Day of Resurrection.
56:50: They will be gathered together at a appointed time on a known day.
56:51: God Almighty says to the people of the left: Then you, O you who have gone astray from the path of guidance, who deny God’s threat and promise, will eat from the tree of Zaqqum.
56:52: You will eat from the trees of Zaqqum
56:53: And His saying, And their bellies will be filled with it, means: And their bellies will be filled with the tree of Zaqqum. The Arabists differed about the reason for the feminization of the tree in his saying: And their bellies will be filled with it meaning from the tree. And they will drink from it because the tree is made feminine and masculine. He made it feminine because he applied it to the tree because the tree may indicate all, so the Arabs say: A bitter tree and a bad herb grew before us, and they mean all. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: They will eat from the tree of Zaqqum.
