And in the reading of Abdullah: They will eat from the tree of Zaqqum it is singular, so the meaning of tree and tree is one because if you say I took from the sheep, then you intend one or more of that, then it is permissible. Then he said: And their bellies will be filled with it, meaning from the tree. If he had said: And they will be filled with it, if he had not mentioned the tree, it would have been correct. He would go to the tree in from it and feminize the tree, so from it would be a metaphor for the tree, and the tree is made feminine and masculine, like the date is made feminine and masculine.
56:54: God Almighty says: Then the people of the left will drink from the tree of Zaqqum when they eat it and fill their bellies with scalding water whose boiling and heat have reached their peaks. It has been said that the meaning of His statement, Then they will drink from it is: They will drink from the tree of Zaqqum when they eat it.
56:55: And his saying, And they will drink the drink of the burning camel, the reciters differed in the recitation of that, so the majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa recited it as the drink of the burning camel with a damma on the shin, and some of the reciters of Mecca, Basra, and Syria recited it as the drink of the burning camel based on the fact that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about the days of Mina: They are days of eating and drinking. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that they are two readings, and each of them has been recited by scholars among the reciters, despite the closeness of their meanings. Whichever of them the reciter recites, he is correct in his recitation, because it is with a fatha, similar to the fatha of their saying: weakness and weakness, and with a damma. As for ilahim, it is the plural of ahaym, and the female is hayma’, and haym is the camel that is afflicted with a disease and is not satisfied with water. Some Arabs say ha’im, and the female is ha’im, then they pluralize it as haym, just as they said a’ayt, a’yit, ha’il, and hawl. It is said that haym is the sand, meaning that the people of Hell drink boiling water as sand drinks water. He mentioned who said about me, like the thirsty camels. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, drinking of thirsty camels, meaning: the drinking of thirsty camels. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And they will drink like thirsty camels. He said: Thirsty camels. Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement, And they will drink like camels drinking water, he said: They are sick camels that suck water continuously but are not satisfied. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, And they will drink like the thirst of thirsty camels. He said: The camels will be seized by thirst and will not stop drinking until they die. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, And they will drink like the thirst of thirsty camels. He said: The camels are seized by thirst and they will not stop drinking until they die. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah: And they will drink like camels drinking. He said: They are the camels that thirsty people drink. He said: Mahran told us on the authority of Sufyan on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They are thirsty camels. Muhammad bin Amr told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, drinking the camels, he said: The camels are the camels. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And they will drink like thirsty camels, “Al-Haym” means thirsty camels that drink and are not quenched by a disease called Al-Hayatim. Bishr told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And they will drink like camels drinking, he said: It is a disease in camels that prevents them from quenching their thirst. Mention of those who said it is Ramla: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan: And they will drink like the drink of the thirsty. He said: The easy way.
56:56: And His statement, This is their lodging on the Day of Judgment, God Almighty says: This that I have described to you, O people, that these deniers who have gone astray eat from the tree of Zaqqum and drink from it scalding water, is their lodging on which their Lord will place them on the Day of Judgment, meaning: the day on which God will judge His servants.
56:57: And His statement, We created you, so why do you not believe? God Almighty says to the infidels of Quraysh and those who denied the al-Qiyamah 75:We created you, O people, and you were nothing, then We made you human beings, so why do you not believe the One who did that to you in His saying to you: He will resurrect you after your death and test you in your graves as you were before your death.
56:58: God Almighty says to those who deny the al-Qiyamah 75:Have you considered, you who deny, God’s ability to revive you after your death, the sperm that you ejaculate in the wombs of your women? Is it you who create that, or are We the creators?
56:59: Do you create it, or are We the creators?
56:60: And His statement, We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outdone. God Almighty says: We have decreed death among you, O people. We hastened it for some and delayed it for others until a specified term. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, We have decreed death among you, he said: The one who is delayed and the one who is hastened. And His statement, And We will not be outdone * In replacing the likes of you, God Almighty says, And We will not be outdone, O people, in yourselves and your appointed times, for they are a trial for us in the matter that We have determined for them of life and death. Rather, nothing of our appointed time can be advanced or delayed.
56:61: And his saying, On the condition that We replace you with others like you, means: On the condition that We replace you with others like you after your destruction, and We bring others of your kind. His statement, And We will produce you in that which you do not know, means: And We will replace what you know of yourselves with forms of yourselves that you do not know. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And We create you, in whatever creation We will.
56:62: God Almighty says: And you have certainly known, O people, the first innovation which We brought about for you, and before that you were nothing. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The first creation, he said: When you were nothing. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And you have certainly known the first creation, meaning the creation of Adam. You will not ask anyone from creation except that he will inform you that God created Adam from clay. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: And you have certainly known the first creation. He said: It is the creation of Adam. Muhammad bin Musa Al-Harsi told me: Jaafar bin Sulayman told us: I heard Abu Imran Al-Joni reciting this verse: And you have certainly known the first creation. He said: It is the creation of Adam. And His saying, Why do you not remember? God Almighty says: Why do you not remember, O people? For you know that He who created you in the first creation, when you were nothing, will not be unable to bring you back to life after your death and annihilation.
56:63: And His statement, Have you seen what you cultivate? God Almighty says: Have you seen, O people, the crops that you cultivate? Is it you who cultivate it, or are We the cultivaters? He says: Do you make it into crops, or are We the ones who make it so? Ahmad bin Al-Walid Al-Qurashi told me: Muslim bin Abi Muslim Al-Harami told us: Mukhallad bin Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Hashim, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not say, ‘I planted,’ but say, ‘I plowed.’” Abu Hurairah said: Have you not heard God’s words: Have you seen what you plow? Is it you who sow it, or are We the sower?
56:64: Do you sow it, or are We the sower?
56:65: God Almighty says: If We willed, We could have made that crop which We planted into debris, meaning chaff that is of no use for food or nourishment. And His saying, And you remained in amazement, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: And you remained astonished at the calamity that befell your crops, with their burning and destruction. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And you remained joking, he said: You were amazed. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And you remained joking. He said: You were amazed. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And you remained joking. He said: You were amazed. Others said: The meaning of this is: You continued to blame each other for your negligence in obeying your Lord, may His praise be glorified, until He brought you what He brought you in terms of destroying your crops. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, And you remained joking, meaning: you were blaming. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak bin Harb Al-Bakri, on the authority of Ikrimah, And you kept joking. He said: You blamed each other. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: You continued to regret what you had done in disobeying God, for which He made His punishment obligatory for you, until it befell you in your crops and what befell you. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told me on the authority of Abu Raja’ on the authority of Al-Hasan: And you remained joking. He said: You regretted. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And you remained joking, he said, you were regretting. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: You remained amazed. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And you remained in a state of amusement, he said, You were amazed at what He did to your sea. And he recited the statement of God Almighty, “Indeed, we are losers. Rather, we are deprived.” And he recited the statement of God, And when they return to their families, they return in a state of amusement. Al-Mutaffifin 31 He said, These are the ones who are at ease. And he recited the statement of God, Most High, So We brought them out from gardens and springs. Al-Shu’ara 57 until His statement, They were therein enjoying themselves. Al-Dukhan 27 The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of those who said: The meaning of so you remained is: So you remained amazed at what had happened to your crops. Its origin is from joking about talking, when a man tells another man a story that amazes him and distracts him, so it is the same. It is as if the meaning of the speech is: So you remained amazed, amazed by one another at what had happened to you.
56:66: And his saying, Indeed, we are infatuated. The people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said: Indeed, we are infatuated with us. Who said that? Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me: Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us: Al-Hussein bin Waqid told me: Yazid Al-Nahwi told me on the authority of Ikrimah regarding the statement of God Almighty, Indeed, we are infatuated, he said: We are infatuated with us. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar: Mujahid said regarding His statement, Indeed, we are infatuated, meaning that he is infatuated with us. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: We are being punished. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, we are in debt means we are being punished. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: We are the ones who cast evil. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Indeed, we are in debt. He said: We will be thrown into evil. The most correct of the sayings is the one that says: It means: We are being tormented. This is because, among the Arabs, grace means torment. From this comes the saying of Al-A’sha: If he punishes with a fine or gives generously, he does not care. What he means by his saying: It will be a loss is: It will be a torment. In the speech, I will suffice with the indication of the speech to it, which is: So you kept joking, saying, We are indeed in love. So he left out saying you are in love from the speech because of what we described.
56:67: And His statement, Rather, we are deprived, means by that, the Most High, that they say: Our crops were not destroyed and we were afflicted with it because of We are indeed losers, but we are a people who are deprived. He says: They are not serious, they have no seriousness. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Rather, we are deprived. He said: We were distorted and thus deprived. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Rather, we are deprived, he said: That is, we are being deviated from.
56:68: God Almighty says: Have you seen, O people, the water that you drink? Is it you who send it down from the clouds above you to the depths of the earth, or is it We who send it down to you? And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of His saying the clouds, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, of the rain clouds, he said: the clouds. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Did you bring it down from the clouds? He said: The clouds are the name of the word you brought it down from the clouds. He said: The clouds. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, You sent it down from the clouds. He said: The clouds are the sky and the rain.
56:69: Is it you who bring it down from the clouds, or are We the bringer down?
56:70: And His statement, If We willed, We could make it bitter. God Almighty says: If We willed, We could make that water which We sent down for you from the clouds salty, which is bitter. And bitter water is the water that is very salty. He says: If We willed, We could do that to it, and you would not benefit from it in drinking, planting, cultivating, or sowing. And His statement, Why do you not give thanks? God Almighty says: Why do you not give thanks to your Lord for giving you what He gave you of fresh water for your drinking, your benefits, and the improvement of your lives, and leaving it brackish so that you do not benefit from it?
56:71: God Almighty says: Have you seen, O people, the fire that you extract from your own firewood? Did you create its tree? He says: Did you create its tree and invent its origin? Or are We the originators? He says: Or did We invent that and invent it? And His saying, We have made it a reminder, means: We have made the fire a reminder for you by which you may be reminded of the fire of Hell, so that you may take heed and learn from it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, A reminder, he said: A reminder of the Great Fire. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Have you seen the fire which you kindle? Was it you who caused its tree to grow, or were We the cause to grow? We made it a reminder of the greater fire. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This fire of yours that you kindle is one part of seventy parts of the fire of Hell. They said: O Prophet of God, is that sufficient? He said: It has been struck with water two or two times so that the children of Adam may benefit from it and come near to it. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, A reminder: He said: For the great fire in the afterlife. And his saying, And provision for the strengthened. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the strengthened. Some of them said: They are the travelers. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, for the strengthened, he said: for the travelers. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And provision for the needy, he said: meaning travelers. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And provision for the needy. He said to the traveler: the one who is weak. Ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, for the strengthened ones, he said: the travelers. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And provision for the needy, that he said: For travelers. Others said: What is meant by the oppressed are those who enjoy it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and provision for the needy for all people who enjoy themselves. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid: And provision for the needy for those who enjoy themselves, whether traveling or staying. Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib Al-Shaheed told me: Atab bin Bishr told us on the authority of Khasif regarding his statement, And a provision for the strong, he said: For creation. Others said: Rather, he meant by that: the hungry. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And provision for the needy, that the one who is needy is the hungry in the speech of the Arabs. He says, I was satisfied with such and such from it, meaning I did not eat such and such a thing from it. The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: What is meant by this is the traveler who has no provisions with him or anything for himself, and its origin is from their saying: The sustenance of the house: if it is empty of its people and inhabitants, as the poet said: Stronger and more desolate than Na'am and others, the raging wind that blows away the dust He means by his saying stronger than its inhabitants. The word stronger may mean strong horse or much money in other places.
56:72: Did you create its tree, or were We the creators?
56:73: We have made it a reminder and a provision for the needy.
56:74: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So glorify, O Muhammad, the remembrance of your Lord, the Great, and His name. And his saying, So I swear by the positions of the stars. The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of his saying, So I swear by the positions of the stars. Some of them said: By his saying, So I swear, he meant: I swear. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muslim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: I do not swear. He said: I swear. Some Arab scholars said: The meaning of his saying No is that the matter is not as you say. Then he resumed the oath after that and it was said I swear. And his saying, By the positions of the stars, the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: Its meaning is that I do not swear by the positions of the Qur’an. They said: The Qur’an was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as scattered stars. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us: Hisin told us, on the authority of Hakim bin Jubair, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Qur’an was revealed on the Night of Decree from the highest heaven to the lowest heaven all at once, then it was distributed throughout the years. He said: Ibn Abbas recited this verse: So I swear by the positions of the stars. He said: It was revealed in separate parts. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, So I swear by the positions of the stars, he said: God revealed the Qur’an in stages, three verses, four verses, and five verses. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah: The entire Qur’an was revealed and placed in the positions of the stars, and Gabriel would recite the surah. It was all revealed on the Night of Decree. Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid: So I swear by the positions of the stars. He said: This is the decisive verse in the Qur’an. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, “So I swear by the positions of the stars. And indeed, it is a great oath, if you but knew.” He said: The place of the Book is its beginning and its end. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that I do not swear by the places where the stars fall. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, in the positions of the stars, he said in the sky, and it is said their risings and their fallings. Bishr told me: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, So I swear by the positions of the stars: meaning their places of occurrence. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: by the mansions of the stars. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: So I swear by the positions of the stars. He said: By the stations of the stars. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: the scattering of the stars at the time of the Hour. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, So I swear by the positions of the stars, he said: Al-Hasan said, their setting and scattering on the Day of Resurrection. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of those who said: The meaning of that is: I do not swear by the places where the stars fall and set in the sky. This is because mawaqe’ is the plural of mawaqe’ and mawaqe’ is the verbal noun from waqa’a, which means waq’a, so the most common of its meanings and the most apparent of its interpretations is what we said on this matter. Therefore we said: This is the most deserving of its meanings. The readers differed in reading this. The majority of the readers of Kufa read it in a position on the unification, and the majority of the readers of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians read it in positions: on the group. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings with one meaning, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.
56:75: I swear by the positions of the stars
56:76: And His statement, And indeed, it is an oath, if you but knew, a great one. God Almighty says, “And indeed, this oath that I have sworn is an oath, if you but knew what it is and its extent. It is a great oath from the deferred, which means to bring forward. Rather, it is: a great oath, if you but knew its greatness.”
56:77: And His saying, Indeed, it is a noble Qur’an, God Almighty says: I swear by the positions of the stars that this Qur’an is a noble Qur’an. The ha in His saying, Indeed is from the mention of the Qur’an.
56:78: And His saying, In a protected book, God Almighty says, It is in a protected book with God, and nothing of harm, such as dust or anything else, touches it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ismail bin Musa told me: Sharik told us, on the authority of Hakim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: None shall touch it except the purified is the book in heaven. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, in a protected book, he said: The Qur’an is in His protected book that is not touched by dust or dirt.
56:79: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, None shall touch it except the purified, that they claimed that the devils brought it down upon Muhammad, so God informed them that they were not able to do that and were not capable of it, and that it was not appropriate for them to bring this down while it was veiled from them. And he recited the statement of God, “And it is not appropriate for them, nor are they able. Indeed, they are removed from hearing” Ash-Shu’ara’ 212. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaid God, meaning Al-Ataki, told us on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid and Abu Nahik regarding his statement, in a protected book, he said: It is a book in the heavens. His statement, None shall touch it except the purified. God Almighty says: None shall touch that hidden Book except those whom God has purified from sins. The interpreters differed about those meant by his saying, except the purified ones. Some of them said: They are the angels. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When God wants to send down a book, the scribes copy it, and none touch it except the purified ones. He said: He means the angels. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Abi Rashid, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr: None shall touch it except the purified ones. He said: The angels in heaven. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Abi Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: None shall touch it except the purified ones. He said: The angels. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Abi Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: None shall touch it except the purified ones. He said: The angels. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaid God, meaning Al-Ataki, told us on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid and Abu Nahik, regarding his statement, None shall touch it except the purified, he said: the angels. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah: None shall touch it except the purified. He said: The angels. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, None shall touch it except the purified, he said: The angels. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah: None shall touch it except the purified ones. He said: The angels. Others said they are the bearers of the Torah and the Gospel. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah: None shall touch it except the purified. He said: The bearers of the Torah and the Gospel. Others said about this: They are those who have been purified from sins, such as the angels and messengers. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Marwan told us: Asim Al-Ahwal told us on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah Al-Riyahi regarding his statement, None shall touch it except the purified, he said: You are not the people of sins. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, None shall touch it except the purified, that he said: The angels, prophets, and messengers who descend from God are purified, and the prophets are purified. So Gabriel descends with it purified, and the messengers to whom it comes are purified. That is why His statement, None shall touch it except the purified, and the angels, prophets, and messengers are from the angels, and the messengers are from the children of Adam. These descend with it purified, and these recite it to the people purified. And God recited, In the hands of scribes, noble and righteous Abasa 30:15-16. He said: In the hands of the angels who count the deeds of the people. Others said about me that none shall touch it except the purified ones. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, None shall touch it except the purified ones, that is with the Lord of the Worlds. As for you, the unclean polytheist and the filthy hypocrite touch it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, None shall touch it except the purified, he said: None shall touch it with God except the purified. As for in this world, the impure Zoroastrian and the filthy hypocrite shall touch it. And he said in the wording of Ibn Mas’ud, None shall touch it except the purified. The correct statement in this regard, in our view, is that God, the Most High, has stated that none shall touch the hidden Book except the purified. He has thus included in His statement the purified ones, and has not specified some over others. Thus, the angels are among the purified ones, and the messengers and prophets are among the purified ones. Everyone who is purified from sins is among those who are excluded. He meant by His statement, except the purified ones.
56:80: And His saying, A revelation from the Lord of the Worlds, means: This Qur’an is a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds. He revealed it from the hidden book. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaid God Al-Atki told us on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid and Abu Nahik regarding his statement, A revelation from the Lord of the worlds, he said: The Qur’an is from that book.
56:81: God Almighty says: Is it by this Qur’an, the report of which I have informed you and related to you its affair, O people, that you speak softly to those who deny it, out of your collusion with them in denying it and disbelieving in it? The people of interpretation differed, and some of them said something similar to what we said about it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Is it this narration that you are in denial of? He said: You want to agree with them in it and to be inclined towards them. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: Are you lying about this hadith? Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Is it this narration that you are doubting? He said: Are you lying and not believing? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, You are deceivers, meaning: liars.
56:82: And His statement, And you make your provision that you lie, means: And you make thanking God for His provision to you a lie. This is like the statement of another speaker: I made my kindness to you a bad thing from you to me, meaning: I made thanking God for my kindness or the reward for my kindness to you a bad thing from you to me. It was mentioned on the authority of Al-Haitham bin Adi that the language of Azd Shanu’ah is ma razaq which means ma zakah what someone was thankful for. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said, with some differences among them. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya told us: Sufyan told us: Abd al-A’la al-Tha’labi told us on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: And you make your provision that you lie. He said: Your gratitude. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Abd Al-A’la Al-Tha’labi, on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Salami, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: And you make your provision that you lie. He said: Your thanks are that you say it rained because of such and such a star and such and such a star. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Yahya bin Abi Bakr told us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: And you make your provision that you lie. He said: Your gratitude is that you lie. He said: They say that it rained because of such and such a star. Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: No people ever receive rain except that some of them become disbelievers, saying, We received rain because of such-and-such a star. Ibn Abbas recited: And you make your provision that you lie. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Atiyah told us: Muadh bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he used to recite: And you make your provision that you deny. Then he said: People have never had rain one night without some of the people becoming polytheists in the morning, saying, ‘We have had rain because of such-and-such a star.’ He said: And you make your gratitude that you deny. Yaqoub told me: Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, And you make your provision, he said: Your thanks for what He sent down upon you of rain and mercy, you say, It rained because of such and such a star. He said, That was from them ingratitude for what He bestowed upon them. Yunus told me: Sufyan told us on the authority of Ismail bin Umayya. I think it was him or someone else. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard a man say when it rained: We were rained upon by some of the lion’s cubs. He said: “You have lied. Rather, it is God’s provision.” Yunus told me, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Verily, God may bless a people in the morning or in the evening, and a people may become disbelievers in the morning because of it, ‘We have been given rain by the star of such and such.’ Muhammad said: “So I mentioned the blessing or He may bless them in the evening, and a people may become disbelievers in the morning because of it, and they say, ‘We have been given rain by the star of such and such.’” Muhammad said: “So I mentioned this hadith to Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, and he said: We have heard it from Abu Hurayrah, and someone told me that he witnessed Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him praying for rain. When he prayed for rain, he turned to al-Abbas and said: ‘O Abbas, O uncle of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), how much of the Pleiades star remains?’ He said: ‘The scholars of it claim that it appears on the horizon seven times after its setting.’ He said: ‘Not even seven days had passed before they had rain.’” Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ali: And you make your provision that you lie. He said: He used to recite it: And you make your gratitude that you lie. He said: You made God’s provision in the stars’ stars, and their provision was in themselves in the stars, the stars of rain. When rain came to them, they said, We were provided with such-and-such a star. But when it was withheld from them, they lied. So that was their denial. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani, regarding his statement, And you make your provision that you lie, he said: There were people who were given rain and they would say, It rained because of such-and-such a star, it rained because of such-and-such a star. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And you make your provision that you lie, he said: Their saying about the signs, Our rain is because of such-and-such a star, means, Say, ‘It is from God, His provision.’ It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And you make your provision that you deny, that God made your provision in the sky, and you make it in the stars. Abu Saleh Al-Sarari told me: Abu Jaber Muhammad bin Abdul Malik Al-Azdi told us: Jaafar bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Umamah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No people receive rain at night except that a group of people become disbelievers in the morning. Then he said: And you make your provision that you lie. He says: “Someone says: ‘We receive rain because of such and such a star.’” Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that you make your share of it denial. Who said that? Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And you make your provision that you deny. As for Al-Hasan, he used to say, “What a bad thing it is that a people have taken for themselves. They have not been provided with anything from the Book of God except the denial of it.” Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar: Al-Hasan said regarding His statement, And you make your provision that you lie, that a servant has lost out whose only share of God’s Book is denial.
56:83: And His statement, Why, then, when it reaches the throat? God Almighty says: Why, then, when the souls, O people, reach your throats, and you at that time are looking on? He says: And whoever of your family is present at them at that time is looking at them. The address here is general to everyone, and what is meant by it is whoever of the family of the deceased is present and others. This is well-known from the speech of the Arabs, which is that a group is addressed by the verb as if they were his family and companions, and what is meant by it is some of them, whether they are absent or present, so he says, You killed so-and-so, and the killer is one of them, either absent or present. We have explained similar examples of this in many places in this book of ours.
56:84: And you will then be watching.
56:85: He says, And We are nearer to him than you. He says, And Our messengers who take his soul are nearer to him than you, but you do not see. Some of the Arab scholars from Basra used to say: It was said, Why, when it reaches the throat, and you are then looking on? It was as if he had heard from them, and God knows best, that we are able not to die. So he said, Why, when it reaches the throat? Then he said, Why, if you are not to be held accountable? That is, not to be able to compensate those souls, and you see how they will come out at that time, if you are truthful in that you are preventing death.
56:86: God Almighty says: Why then, O people, if you were not indebted? The people of interpretation differed regarding his statement, debted. Some of them said, not accountable. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us on the authority of Ali on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Then why, if you were not to be held accountable, he means not to be held accountable. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, not being held accountable, he said, not being held accountable. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Why, if you were not to be judged, he said: They denied that they would be judged after death. He said: And He is the Master of the Day of Judgment, the day when people will be judged for their deeds. He said: They will be judged: they will be held accountable. Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Abu Raja’ told us on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, Then why, if you were not to be held accountable, he said, not to be held accountable. Ibn Bashar told us: Sulayman told us: Abu Hilal told us on the authority of Qatada: Why, if you were not to be judged? He said: Not resurrected and not held accountable. Others said that it means not being sent. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Hudha told us, he said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Then why, if you are not to be recompensed - not to be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, you will return it if you are truthful. Others said: Rather, it means that you are not rewarded for your deeds. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of those who said: They will not be held accountable, but will be rewarded for your deeds, based on their saying, As you judge, you will be judged, and on the saying of God, Owner of the Day of Judgment (al-Fatihah 1:4).
56:87: And His statement, You will return them, if you are truthful, means: You will return those souls after their destination is the throats to their final resting place in the bodies, if you are truthful, if you are abstaining from death, accountability, and recompense. The answer to His statement, Then why, when it reaches the throat, and the answer to His statement, Then why, if you are not to be held accountable, is one answer, which is His statement, You will return them, and that is similar to His statement, But if there comes to you guidance from Me, then whoever follows My guidance will have no fear (al-Baqarah 2:38). He made the answer to the two recompenses one answer. And in a similar manner to what we said about His statement, You will return it, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, You will return it, He said to that soul, If you are truthful.
56:88: And His statement, But if he was among those brought near, * then there is comfort and fragrance. God Almighty says: But if the deceased was among those brought near whom God brought near to be near Him in His Paradise, then there is comfort and fragrance. He says, He has comfort and fragrance. The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of reciters in the regions read it as farooh with a fatha on the ra’, meaning he has coolness, and basil meaning and abundant provision according to some of them, and according to others he has comfort and basil. Al-Hasan al-Basri read it as farooh with a damma on the ra’, meaning that his soul comes out in basil. The first of the two readings is the correct one, which reads it with the fat-ha, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it, meaning: For Him is mercy, forgiveness, and good and pleasant provision. The commentators differed in their interpretation of his statement, A place of rest and relaxation. Some of them said: It means comfort and rest. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Farooh and basil means comfort and rest. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, But if he is of those brought near, * There will be comfort and basil. He said, Blessings means the one who is relieved from this world. And a Garden of Delights means forgiveness and mercy. Others said that the soul is comfort and basil is sustenance. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And rest and fragrance, he said: Rest. And his statement, And fragrance, he said: Provision. Others said: The spirit means joy and basil means sustenance. Abu Kuraib told us: Idris told us: I heard my father, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr, regarding his statement, And comfort and basil, he said: Comfort means joy and basil means provision. As for those who read it with a damma on the ra’, they said: The soul is the soul of the human being and the basil is the well-known basil. They said that the meaning of this is that the souls of those close to God leave their bodies at death with basil that you smell. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Hasan: Farooh and basil. He said: His soul comes out in his basil. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah: But if he is among those brought near, he said: There is no one among those brought near and those brought near who are the foremost until he is given some of the basil of Paradise and smells it, then he dies. Others who read it with the opening of the letter ra said: The spirit means mercy and the basil means the well-known basil. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Spirit and basil. He said: The spirit is mercy and basil is what he receives at death. Others said that the spirit is mercy and the basil is rest. Who said that? Al-Hussein told us that he heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us that he heard Al-Dahhak say: Farooh and basil. The spirit means forgiveness and mercy, and basil means rest. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Mundhir al-Thawri, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim: But if he is among those brought near he said: This is at death then there is comfort and fragrance he said: It will be brought to him from Paradise. Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Amir told us: Qurra told us on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement, But if he is among those brought near, then there is comfort and basil and a Garden of Delight, he said that in the Hereafter, so some of the people said to him, he said: By God, they will see at death. Ibn Bashar told us: Hammad told us: Qurra told us on the authority of Al-Hasan, with a similar narration. The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said about me by the spirit: joy, mercy, and forgiveness. Its origin is from their saying: I found a spirit, if he found a breeze to which he could breathe from the distress of the heat. As for basil, in my opinion it is the basil that is received at death, as Abu al-Aaliyah and al-Hasan said, and whoever said something similar to their saying, because that is the most common and most apparent of its meanings. And his saying, And a garden of pleasures, means: He also has a garden of pleasures in which he can enjoy himself. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said: A paradise of bliss. He said: It was shown to him.
56:89: Spirit, basil, and a garden of delights
56:90: God Almighty says: “But if the deceased is one of the companions of the right hand, who will be taken to Paradise on their right hands, then peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand.” Then there was a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of his saying, “Peace be upon you from the companions of the right.” The people of interpretation said about it what: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, “But if he is among the companions of the right hand, then peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand.” He said: Peace be upon the servant of God, and the angels of God greeted him. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, “But if he is from the companions of the right hand, then peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand,” that is, it is said, “Peace be upon you.” Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: His statement, “Then peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand,” that is, it is confirmed to you that you are from the companions of the right hand. That was omitted and its meaning was intended, as you say, You are a traveler who has been confirmed in a short while, and you are a traveler who has been confirmed in a short while. He said: His statement, “Then peace be upon you,” means: “Peace be upon you, you are from the companions of the right hand.” He said: It may be like a supplication for him, like his statement, A drink for you from the men. He said: If you raise the greeting, then it is a supplication, and God knows best which is correct. Others said, among them is his statement, But if he is among those brought near, for he combined two answers to show that but is a reward. He said: As for his statement, “Then peace be upon you from the companions of the right,” he said: This is the root of the word, This is Muslim to you, then that was deleted and from was used in its place. He said: It has been said: “Then peace be upon you, you are among the companions of the right,” so it is like that: meaning, peace be upon you. It is said: You are among the companions of the right, and all of this is based on two statements. He said: It has been said: Muslim, meaning just as you say: “Then peace be upon you from the people,” just as you say: Then a drink for you from the people, so it becomes one statement. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: Its meaning is: Peace be upon you, for you are among the companions of the right hand. Then he omitted and dared to indicate that it was on her, so you were saved from the punishment of God and from what you dislike because you are among the companions of the right hand.
56:91: "Peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand."
56:92: And His statement, But if he was among the deniers and the astray, * then he will be given scalding water. God Almighty says: But if the deceased was among those who denied the signs of God and deviated from His path, then he will be given scalding water that has been boiled until its heat reaches its utmost limit, and that is his drink.
56:93: Then he sent down scalding water.
56:94: And the burning of Hellfire He says: And the burning of Hellfire with which he burns. And the burning is the active participle from the prayer of God to the Fire, so he burns him with a burning, and that is if he burns him with it.
56:95: God Almighty says: Indeed, what I have informed you of, O people, regarding the report of those brought near to God, the companions of the right hand, and the deniers who have gone astray, and what their affairs will eventually lead to, is the certain truth. He says: It is the certain truth of the report, there is no doubt about it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Indeed, this is the certain truth. He said: The certain report. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: “But if he is among the deniers and the astray, then he will be sent with scalding water and will be burned in Hellfire. Indeed, this is the certainty of truth.” Until he concluded: God Almighty will not leave anyone of His creation until He makes him stand on certainty of this Qur’an. As for the believer, he is certain in this world, and that will benefit him on the Day of Resurrection. As for the disbeliever, he is certain on the Day of Resurrection when it will not benefit him. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for adding the truth to certainty, and the truth is certainty. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He said: The truth of certainty, so he added the truth to certainty, just as he said, That is the upright religion Al-Bayyinah 5, meaning that is the religion of the upright religion, and that is the truth of the certain matter. He said: As for this evil man, there is no evil in this man as there is in the truth of certainty, because the black man is not the man, and certainty is the truth. Some of the people of Kufa said: Certainty is an attribute of the truth, as if he said: The truth is certainty and the upright religion, and something similar has come in many speeches and the Qur’an, And for the home of the Hereafter Yusuf 109 - An-Nahl 30, And for the home of the Hereafter Al-A’raf 169 - Al-Ahzab 29. He said: So if it is added, something other than the first is imagined.
56:96: And His saying, So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great, God Almighty says: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great, with His beautiful names.
